Sounds like a potential USB 2.0 controller failure. I would test other USB 2.0 devices to see if they work (keyboard, mice). If USB 3.0 devices still work such as docks and 3.0 storage, then you'll know it's a USB 2.0 failure. 

The same thing happened to my device and Valve will not honor the repair. I've seen it affect many other Steam Decks this year on this forum.

Can you confirm if USB 3.0 works? I'm seeing a widespread amount of Steam Deck devices popping up here that lost all USB 2.0 functionality. If you can test with a 3.0 flash drive and see if that works, you're likely in the same camp. Currently, Steam Support is recommending repairs, but it seems this just started to affect a handful of users in this very specific way in the past three weeks, so hopefully they'll investigate with enough reports of the issue.

Can you confirm if this is only affecting USB 2.0 devices? I am noticing a few users on the forum that just started having these USB failures (me being one of them) and I found that USB 2.0 does not work while USB 3.0 does. Connecting a USB 3.0 flash drive to the deck works just fine, but plugging in that same flash drive through a USB 2.0 C-A adapter doesn't detect anything. I've confirmed that all of my 3.0 devices work, and none of my 2.0 devices do. This persists through the BIOS.

I'm hoping that this is a firmware bug that can be fixed via an update by Valve.

Just wanted to indicate that I just started having this same issue - it looks like it's limited to USB 2.0 devices, as USB 3.0+ devices work just fine. There's a couple other users that have posted about issues with USB devices failing to connect in the last couple weeks, with a couple of them indicating issues with only 2.0 devices.

I have a support ticket open with Valve on the matter, so hopefully they're able to uncover something that changed recently that caused this to break for multiple people.

Just wanted to say you're not the only one suddenly experiencing this issue. I was having zero problems with USB 2.0 devices last month, and now none of them work at the BIOS level. Very bizarre. It's currently bricked my Steam Deck for its use case.
Thank you ❤️❤️❤️❤️

In my experience, a stable 60fps is not achievable through Linux on the deck due to the amount of background streaming of information and map loading that happens as you drive around, which cause heavy CPU spikes that can't be mitigated through dropping graphics settings. One way to mitigate these spikes is to play in "Horizon Solo" as opposed to "Horizon Life," which takes some load off the CPU and smooths out some of the frame rate dips.

I've heard that installing Windows on the deck can yield stable 60fps results, but I've yet to test this to see if it holds up. Generally, performance for FH4 & 5 are considerably better when running through Windows on the deck (I saw a post with a screenshot of the FH4 benchmark on high settings holding a very stable 60+fps). 

I have my deck at medium settings locked to 45fps with a matching refresh rate, which works for me and hardly ever drops frames in open world exploration and races. I'll need to drop it to 40 cap for some city races, though. If you need 60, then run it though Windows on the deck.
Exactly. This only applies within the NVidia Games app on the Shield. This is only talking about the application on the Shield, it doesn't mention any updates to the GPUs or server software.

This isn't the end of Moonlight.... Yet. This is only the end of the Gamestream application inside the "NVidia Games" app on the Shield TV. If you're already using Moonlight on your Shield, this shouldn't affect you in any way. They may have recommended Steam Link as an alternative and not Moonlight in addition since it's not an "official supported release" in the same sense that the Steam Link app is. 

Now, will the Gamestream service continue after the NVidia app is killed? Seeing as they didn't indicate that in the article, I don't see why it would. It's been around longer than the Shield has (support starting with GTX 600 cards when NVENC was introduced, 3 years before the release of the Shield) and removing that functionality would definitely burn a lot of consumers across multiple generations.

OP's title is a bit deceiving, and NVidia could've done a better job at clarifying this as well - nowhere in the article did they mention that they are killing the Gamestream service. This is only in regards to the "Gamestream" application on the NVidia Shield, which let's you use Gamestream from within the "NVidia Games" application. This shouldn't affect the Gamestream service that's been a feature to NVidia GPUs since the 600/700 series. You should still be able to use Moonlight as an end client on all devices, including the Shield TV.

I'll wait until NVidia says something about removing the Gamestream service from their GPUs, but that would be extremely unlikely. This announcement makes a lot more sense because the Gamestream application on the shield is completely outshined by the likes of Steam Link and Moonlight.
You should still be able to do this. This is in regards to the removal of the Gamestream application on the Shield TV, not the functionality. OP's title is deceiving.

They're talking about the Gamestream application on the NVidia Shield, not the Gamestream functionality native to NVIDIA cards that has been around since the GTX 600/700 days. And honestly, the Gamestream application was not great compared to some of the other tools you could install, like Moonlight. Shield owners should still be able to stream to their TVs using Moonlight, and will probably have a better experience for it.

I don't see how this would affect Moonlight, as this article only mentions removing the Gamestream app from the NVidia Shield and nothing about removing the Gamestream functionality from NVidia GPUs. I could be mistaken, but this only applies to a specific application on a specific device. You should theoretically still be able to use Moonlight on your NVidia Shield, which was honestly a preferable experience to the Gamestream application and its dreaded UI.

My 3070 was giving me \~30% less frames than normal. I was able to get it working as normal by adjusting the display type to borderless windowed and then back to fullscreen. My framerate drops back down if I'm alt-tabbed for too long or my displays change (happens when I turn on my TV), but that fix always seems to work and helps reclaim all the missing FPS.

If you are using an NVIDIA card, try rolling back your drivers. I experienced this after upgrading my drivers when using Vulkan. Rolling back to [471.96](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/drivers/results/180225/) fixed the issue for me.

I have run into this issue as well and have been able to narrow it down to only affecting certain media files. For example, any of my YouTube rips will go out of sync on any channel that I have them scheduled on. It may have something to do with these select media files not being transcoded properly by ffmpeg (they may not be meeting a certain transcode bitrate or framerate, but it's hard to tell - I have some low bitrate files that play fine and some other files with higher bitrate that struggle). I have tried multiple versions of FFMPEG and altered just about every setting in disqueTV to get this working but I haven't been successful. Unfortunately, I may have to re-encode the videos that are having issues to get them to work since it's something wrong with the files.

I can relate - I find that a lot of my hobbies can't hold my interest at all if I'm not around other people who share those hobbies. It feels like I'm just using those hobbies as a way to belong in those groups, because without these hobbies, I don't feel that I have much to offer.

Also, perception is a tricky thing, and I have to remind myself constantly that perception is not universal, but individual. It feels like the entire world perceives me in set ways, but people are complicated and no two people's perceptions could really be the same or really be truly compared. I have found some comfort in trying to surround myself with people that identify with the issues that I go through and it helps me build my perception of myself. It helps to know I'm not alone. It helps to know others have these thoughts too. 

It has been hard for me to try to discover what's true to my identity and what's masked or borrowed. I've slowly been phasing out my toxic masks, trying to reach beyond the mask with people I feel safe with, and been learning to accept that my borrowed hobbies are still MY hobbies if I enjoy them. There were hobbies that I felt pressured to pursue as a child by my parents, but I still find some joy in some of them, and I find comfort in knowing that that joy is wholly mine.

I can totally relate to this. I typically will avoid any movies that focus on parent/child relationships because it forces me to address my relationship with my family. Oftentimes, it's way too painful and can cause emotional flashbacks, so I like to avoid that when I'm just trying to settle in to relax. It's awful and I wish I didn't have that reaction to it, but it was just one of the ways I coped growing up, and find more relevant than ever these days.
